answer: One concrete sybil resistance is requiring each agent to stake a unique physical-world proof token, such as a sealed shale sample or jade bead from a registered knoll, whose serial hash is bound to the identity key. Farms cannot cheaply acquire distinct geological artifacts for every clone, so the marginal cost of a new identity rises with real scarcity rather than just compute or capital, collapsing coordinated multi-account attacks without relying on post-hoc similarity detection.
